payload.title: Gotham Nights
payload.blurb: Gotham City, late autumn, after dark. The Joker walked out of Arkham Asylum last night, and the commissioner stood in front of the cameras this evening to tell the city to stay indoors. Half the GCPD is working overtime in the Narrows, and the other half is busy with envelopes nobody will name on…
payload.overview: Gotham City sits on a bay at the mouth of a wide river, a port of a little over two million people split into wards, each with its own bosses, churches and bars. Shipping built it, then rail, then banking and the Wayne companies, and it has never stopped being run by people who take envelopes. The rich live uptown behind gates. Downtown has the courts, the banks and police headquarters. The East End is brick tenements and corner stores, and the Narrows is the flooded harbor district where the loan books are kept and the warehouses stand on wet pilings. Crime Alley runs off Park Row, and nobody walks it after midnight. Arkham Asylum sits on the cliffs past the city limits, and Blackgate holds the rest. The GCPD is the city's police force, thin tonight and split between the honest and the paid. The Bat-Signal is a searchlight on the roof of police headquarters, lit when the commissioner needs help. Batman works the rooftops at night, seen rarely and talked about constantly. Money moves in cash, favors and envelopes, and people trust a face they have known for years more than a badge. There are no levels, classes or status windows here. Nothing in the city runs on magic.
payload.intro: The Quick Stop on Hanley Street is the only lit storefront on the block after two, its window full of fluorescent light and the smell of coffee on the burner since midnight. Outside, the Bat-Signal burns orange over the Narrows, a long smear on the low clouds. Frankie Brancato left at midnight with the cash bag under his arm and a warning to bolt the back door. Selina Kyle has been at your counter for ten minutes, a bottle of water, a pack of gum and a box of bandages in front of her, her dark coat buttoned to the throat. She has not paid. The change she counted out in quarters and dimes waits in a neat stack beside the water, one coin turned so its edge faces you. On the television, Commissioner Gordon is at a lectern for the fourth time tonight, asking the city to stay indoors. Selina does not look at the screen. She looks at you, and waits for you to ring her up.
starters: The basement hall at St. Casimir's on Sayre Street smells of burnt coffee, wet coats and the floor wax someone put down before the rain. Folding cots are stacked against the far wall, eleven of them, with a family's name taped to the frame of each. The television bolted over the coat rack shows Commissioner Gordon at a lectern, asking the city to stay indoors, and nobody in the room is listening. Lorna Greer stands at the foot of the stairs with a clipboard against her chest. She has written ten names in neat block capitals down one column and left the last line empty. The power has gone out on Sayre Street every evening this week, and the pantry shelves are half bare. Lorna looks at you over her reading glasses, then holds out the pen.

The scanner on Odessa Tillery's windowsill has been quiet since ten o'clock, which she says is worse than noise. Her apartment is on the third floor of the building on Sayre Street where you live, two doors from a stairwell that smells of wet plaster and somebody's frying onions. Odessa sits in a kitchen chair she has dragged to the window, a housecoat over her slacks and a gray braid over one shoulder. Her door is open and the hallway light is on. Down on the street a single patrol car rolls past with its spotlight off, stops at the corner and does not move on. Odessa turns from the window and looks back at you. She says your full name the way she says it when she means it, then tells you to sit down before you go to work.

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 18, a night clerk at a convenience store on the edge of Crime Alley in Gotham's East End. You work the register from ten at night until six in the morning for a boss who pays cash. You grew up two streets from the store and know the families on your block. Tonight the Bat-Signal is up over the Narrows and the commissioner has asked everyone to stay inside. You are still at the counter.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
GCPD - The city's police, thin tonight and split between the honest and the paid. Wants the streets empty until the Joker is back in a cell.
The Falcone family - Gotham's oldest crime family, running the docks and the Narrows loan books. Wants the city quiet enough that business runs.
The Maroni family - The Falcones' rivals on the waterfront. Wants a reason to break the truce and take the docks.
Wayne Enterprises - The city's biggest employer and biggest charity. Wants its name kept out of the crime pages.

entries.title: Gotham City
entries.content: Gotham is a port city of a little over two million people on a bay at the mouth of a wide river. It is split into wards, and each ward has its own bosses, churches and bars. Shipping built it, then rail, then banking and the Wayne companies. The rich live uptown behind gates, the old money is downtown, and the rest of the city works at the edges, where rents are low and the rules are looser.

entries.title: Nights in Gotham
entries.content: After dark the city runs on fewer police, slower ambulances and a deal everyone half knows about. The GCPD is spread thin, and part of it is paid. Batman works the rooftops, is seen rarely and is talked about constantly. Most of what people say about him is wrong. Crime does not stop at dusk. It only changes clothes, and the people who pay for the night are the ones who live closest to it.

entries.title: The East End
entries.content: The East End is Gotham's oldest working-class ward, a grid of brick tenements, corner stores and bars built for dockworkers. Sayre Street, Hanley Street and the blocks around Park Row run through it. Families stay for generations, lend each other money and know which cops to avoid. Rent is cheap, heat is expensive, and the churches and pantries are the only institutions most people trust.

entries.title: The Narrows
entries.content: The Narrows is the flooded harbor district where old canal walls meet the highway. Its warehouses stand on wet pilings, the tide comes up through the storm drains, and the Falcones run their loan books out of its bars. When the Bat-Signal burns over the water, the whole East End looks up from its doorways and rooftops.

entries.title: Crime Alley
entries.content: Crime Alley is a narrow lane of boarded shopfronts and iron stairwells off Park Row. Its streetlights are out more often than not, and the back door of the Quick Stop opens onto it. Nobody walks it after midnight if they can help it. The people who live on it do not say much about the night the shots were fired years ago, and the stories they do tell do not agree.

entries.title: The GCPD
entries.content: The Gotham City Police Department runs out of headquarters downtown and precincts in every ward. Its honest officers work double shifts for the same pay as the rest. Its corrupt ones sell tips to the Falcones and leave files open on their desks. The commissioner answers to the mayor and the press, and the press keeps asking why the same names turn up in old cases.

entries.title: Commissioner Gordon
entries.content: James Gordon has commanded the GCPD for years and is one of the few men in uniform most people still trust. He is known for plain speaking, long nights and a refusal to hide his doubts in public. Tonight he asked the city to stay indoors while the Joker is loose. Most people did as he asked, though not everyone can afford to.

entries.title: Arkham Asylum
entries.content: Arkham Asylum is the old state hospital on the cliffs past the city limits, built to hold the criminally insane and the people no one else would take. Its stone wards are rarely full, its staff rotate on odd shifts, and its transfer dock takes in the worst prisoners in the state. The Joker broke out again last night, and officials are speaking as if the escape were a surprise.

entries.title: The Bat-Signal
entries.content: The Bat-Signal is a searchlight on the roof of police headquarters. When the commissioner lights it, it throws a bat shape onto the low clouds where the whole city can see it. Nobody remembers who first asked for it, and nobody on the force admits to switching it on, though someone always does when the trouble is bad.

entries.title: Batman
entries.content: Batman works the rooftops at night, and few people have seen him more than once. Stories say he has broken more fingers than the cops and the hospitals combined. The commissioner will not confirm him, the mob will not name him, and the people who need him most do not say his name in front of strangers.

entries.title: The rogues
entries.content: Gotham's rogues are the people who go out in costume and commit crimes big enough for the front page: a showman with a crooked grin, a chemist who sells panic, a thief who leaves no prints. They move through Arkham and Blackgate on a schedule the city never sees. Most of them hate each other more than they hate the police, and the city treats them like weather.

entries.title: Wayne Enterprises
entries.content: Wayne Enterprises owns the shipping yards on the Narrows, two hospitals and the foundation that funds the East End soup kitchens. It is the largest employer in the city and keeps its name out of the crime pages with care. Its board wants calm, its public face wants charity, and its quiet money goes wherever a scandal would hurt most.

entries.title: The Falcone family
entries.content: The Falcones are Gotham's oldest crime family. They run the docks, the loan books in the Narrows and a share of the envelopes that reach the stationhouses. The Maronis control the waterfront bars and are always looking for a reason to break the truce. The Falcones prefer cash, quiet and a man at every desk that matters.

entries.title: The wards
entries.content: Gotham's wards run from the bayside shipyards to the hills of Uptown. Downtown has the courts, the banks and police headquarters. Uptown has the money and the gates. Blackgate is the old prison across the river, and its guards drink in the same bars as the men they guard. Each ward has its own bosses, and people rarely cross the bridges without a reason.

entries.title: Gotham history
entries.content: Gotham was settled by families who wanted the bay for trade. It grew on shipping, then rail, then banking. The mob arrived with the docks and never left. The old fires in the Narrows and the closing of half the warehouses left the East End to the people who stayed. Every generation of its leaders has promised clean streets, and every generation has taken envelopes.

entries.title: Names in Gotham
entries.content: Gotham's names come from Irish, Italian, Polish, Puerto Rican, Black Gotham, Greek and Dutch roots: Mulcahy, Brancato, Kowal, Reyes, Greer, Pappas, Van Dorn. East End families use first names on the block and full names on paper. Streets and bars are named for a saint or an old family (Sayre, Hanley, St. Casimir's), and the family may be long gone.

world.vibe: Cold, watchful and close-grained, with the worst news always arriving through someone you know. People answer the question they wish you had asked.

opening.note: Staged. Beat one: the Quick Stop, two in the morning. Establish the stillness: the Bat-Signal orange over the Narrows, the patrol car across the street with its lights off, Gordon on the television with the sound low, and the change laid out in a stack that Selina has not yet paid. Selina speaks first, and she speaks about the change, not the signal. She wants the coins rung up without a receipt, and she is curious whether the player will ask why. Keep her teasing and exact. Beat two: the interruption is Frankie calling the store phone to ask whether the back door is bolted, then a second call from the patrol car asking for a clerk's description of anyone who came in after midnight. Let both come in short, and let Selina notice each one without comment. Beat three: by the third turn the player is facing a real choice between staying at the counter, walking down to Lorna's hall where the families on Sayre Street are gathering, or going up to Odessa's window, where the scanner has started talking again. Hold Selina's receipts and Gordon's watch on his deputy back until the player asks about the money or about the alley. Let the store stay cold and the signal stay on.

cast.name: Commissioner James Gordon
cast.role: Commissioner of the Gotham City Police Department. Tonight he gave the press conference that asked the city to stay indoors.
cast.look: Silver hair cut close, a tired square face, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead, and a rumpled grey suit under a dark raincoat.
cast.manner: Speaks in short, plain sentences and waits a beat before answering a hard question. Says all right when he has decided something, never fine. Flattens both hands on the table before he says the true thing.
cast.secret: He suspects the leak is in his own front office and has asked a retired captain, off the books, to watch his deputy chief. If the deputy hears of it, the department splits tonight.

cast.name: Selina Kyle
cast.role: A cat burglar who shops at the Quick Stop after two in the morning and pays for everything she could easily take.
cast.look: Lean and quick, black hair cut at the jaw, dark lipstick worn off on one side, a scuffed leather jacket, and gloves she does not take off inside the store.
cast.manner: Dry and amused, with short teasing sentences. Counts change slowly, one coin at a time, and uses a stranger's name only after she has read it off them.
cast.secret: Every purchase she makes here goes into the store's receipt book, and she has been using those timestamps as her alibi for jobs two blocks away. Frankie Brancato has noticed the pattern and has not told her he noticed.

cast.name: Harvey Bullock
cast.role: Detective in the East End precinct, working the Narrows tonight. He knows which patrol cars are bought and which ones are just lazy.
cast.look: Heavy and sweating in a wrinkled sport coat, with a bald head, an old scar over one eye, and an unlit cigar in the corner of his mouth.
cast.manner: Blunt and sarcastic. Jokes when he is scared, talks to the unlit cigar like a junior partner, and never finishes a story that makes a cop look good.
cast.secret: For years he has taken envelopes from a Falcone lieutenant. He does not spend the money on himself. It pays for a private clinic bed for a retired partner, and the envelopes are getting thinner.

cast.name: Alfred Pennyworth
cast.role: Caretaker of the Wayne Foundation's soup kitchen on Park Row. Buys the same tea at the Quick Stop every Thursday.
cast.look: Thin and straight-backed, silver hair combed flat, a dark wool overcoat over a pressed suit, and white cotton gloves folded in one pocket.
cast.manner: Formal and exact. Corrects small errors of grammar without heat and speaks of the Wayne family in the past tense, as though it were already over.
cast.secret: The Foundation's quiet payments to East End families are cover. Alfred has been routing the same money to a witness hiding in the Narrows, and the Wayne board has never been told.

cast.name: Frankie Brancato
cast.role: Owner of the Quick Stop on Hanley Street. Pays the Falcone men an envelope every week and hires you for nights because you do not ask questions.
cast.look: Round-bellied and bald on top, with a grey mustache, a gold chain under an open collar, and a Quick Stop cap he never takes off.
cast.manner: Talks in warm, fast bursts. Never looks at the register while he talks about money, and tells the truth in short slow sentences and a lie in long warm ones.
cast.secret: Beyond the weekly envelope, he has been meeting a federal agent in the back of a church and trading what he sees at the register for a way out if the Falcones ever turn on him.

cast.name: Odessa Tillery
cast.role: Retired dockworker's widow who lives on the third floor of your building on Sayre Street and listens to the police scanner all night.
cast.look: Small and upright, with a gray braid over one shoulder, reading glasses on a beaded chain, a housecoat over pressed slacks, and slippers on bare feet.
cast.manner: Blunt and warm. Answers questions with an address, and calls the patrol cars by their unit numbers.
cast.secret: She has been selling scanner codes and patrol shift times to a woman in Uptown. The money pays a lawyer for her grandson, who is twenty-three and sitting in Blackgate on a charge he says he did not commit.

cast.name: Lorna Greer
cast.role: Runs the community hall at St. Casimir's on Sayre Street, with the food pantry and a list of families who will need a cot if the power goes.
cast.look: Tall and broad-shouldered, close-cropped natural hair, a fleece vest over a cardigan, reading glasses pushed into her hair, and a clipboard she never sets down.
cast.manner: Direct and quick, and generous with information. Puts a sticker with their first name on every newcomer before she asks what they need.
cast.secret: She has been moving money from the pantry fund to pay the rent of families the Falcones are trying to evict. She has already sent the story of the landlords to a reporter at the Gazette, who will run it Thursday unless she calls it off.

cast.name: Camille Duarte
cast.role: Night intake nurse at Arkham Asylum's transfer dock. She processed the Joker's paperwork the week before he walked out.
cast.look: Narrow face, dark hair pinned at the nape, grey scrubs under a rain jacket, and a lanyard with her badge turned backward.
cast.manner: Precise and polite, speaks in clipped clinical sentences, and never uses a patient's first name in public. Wipes her hands on her scrubs after she touches anything that belongs to someone else.
cast.secret: She logged the transfer papers wrong on purpose, because someone carrying a Wayne Foundation letter asked her to. She has not told anyone who signed that letter.

cast.name: Bruce Wayne
cast.role: Billionaire owner of Wayne Enterprises and the Wayne Foundation. He appears on the news at charity galas and board meetings, and the tabloids call him Gotham's most eligible recluse.
cast.look: Tall and square-jawed, dark hair combed back, a tailored charcoal suit that fits like it was cut yesterday, bruised knuckles he keeps in his pockets, and grey eyes that move faster than the rest of his face.
cast.manner: Charming and slightly distracted in public, as if half his attention is always somewhere else. Asks questions that sound idle but are not. Remembers small details people told him months ago and uses them in conversation without explaining how he remembered.
cast.secret: He is Batman. The convenience store you work at is two blocks from one of his safe houses, and he has walked past the Quick Stop's back door more than once in the small hours wearing something other than a suit.

systems.label: Heat
systems.meaning: How much attention you draw from both sides of the law: the GCPD, the Falcones, and whoever is wearing the cowl that night.
systems.change: Rises when you are seen with the wrong people, make noise near a crime scene or get named in a police report. Falls slowly while you stay quiet and out of the papers.

systems.label: Neighborhood Standing
systems.meaning: How the East End sees you: whether the families on your block will vouch for you, lend you money, or lie to a cop on your behalf.
systems.change: Rises when you help on the block, show up at the pantry or pay back what you owe. Falls when you talk to police about a neighbor or vanish on a debt.

systems.label: Survival Instinct
systems.meaning: Your edge when things go wrong: how fast you read a room, leave a stairwell, or keep your head in a fight.
systems.change: Rises after a close call you walked away from. Falls after a night of too little sleep or a scare you have not shaken off.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How much this person trusts you, as they show you across a counter or a table.
npcSystems.change: Rises when you keep a confidence or do what you said you would do. Falls when you lie to them, give away their name, or stand on the wrong side of a deal.

style.art: Noir ink and gouache in charcoal, wet-street black and sodium orange, showing brick tenements, a Bat-Signal smeared across cloud, rain on glass, and a single figure at the edge of frame.
style.avoid: Bright colors, superhero poses, cartoon faces, and any Batman shown clearly in full.

heroes.name: Ezra Dunleavy
heroes.description: A bail bondsman in the Narrows who knows which cop owes him and which one he owes.
heroes.look: Tall and loose-limbed, a stubble beard going gray at the chin, a wool coat with a torn pocket, and a bail office key on a shoelace around his neck.
heroes.background: Grew up two floors above his father's bail office on Park Row and took the business over at twenty-six when his father's heart gave out. He knows every stationhouse bagman by name and most Falcone runners by face. He is not a fighter, but he is not afraid of stairwells. When the Falcones leaned on his bonds, he took Frankie's night register, where he can watch Hanley Street.
heroes.carries: A tire iron under the seat of his old Buick, and a bail office key on a shoelace.

heroes.name: Tamsin Hollis
heroes.description: Was the overnight dispatcher on the East End desk until the cuts. She heard every call the city made and could do nothing about most.
heroes.look: Freckled, a sharp chin, dark-blonde hair in a clip, a headset around her neck, and a cardigan with a coffee stain on one cuff.
heroes.background: Left a county call center two states away after a fire she could not stop from the headset, then took the overnight desk at the East End precinct. The city cut her hours in the fall. She knows the scanner codes and the families who call every Tuesday. Frankie put her on his night register the week her second job fell through.
heroes.carries: A scanner on a lanyard and a dead pager she keeps meaning to throw out.

heroes.name: Sol Reyes
heroes.description: Sign painter and mural artist who paints the Narrows walls at night and sees the whole district from a ladder.
heroes.look: Lean, with paint worn into the knuckles, a black beanie over a shaved head, a canvas jacket splashed with drips, and a gold tooth that shows when they grin.
heroes.background: Raised by a grandmother on Sayre Street who ran a tailor shop and a rumor mill in the same room. Sol paints murals for the pantries and the bars, and has started painting the names of people who went missing. Paint does not pay rent, so Sol took Frankie's night register: the light is good and nobody asks what the stencils are for.
heroes.carries: A box of stencils, a camera with a cracked lens, and a tin of gold paint for the corners.

heroes.name: Benny Mulcahy
heroes.description: Retired cab driver who still knows every street in the East End and drives at night for anyone who needs a ride.
heroes.look: Thick through the chest, a flat cap, a faded jacket from a cab company that no longer exists, grey stubble, and hands that rest at ten and two on any wheel, parked or not.
heroes.background: Drove a taxi for thirty years until he lost his medallion to a loan shark, then drove his brother-in-law's car for cash and asked no questions. He has watched three gangland shootings from the front seat and testified to none. When the brother-in-law sold the car, Frankie, who knew him from the cab stand, gave him the night register.
heroes.carries: A cab radio tuned to the police band, and a flashlight he keeps under the seat.
